overview: HIV is a virus that attacks the body’s immune system, and if left untreated, can progress to AIDS. HIV targets the body’s white blood cells, weakening the immune system, making it easier to get sick with diseases like tuberculosis, infections and some cancers. With access to effective HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care, HIV infection has become a manageable chronic health condition.
symptoms: cancers such as lymphomas and Kaposi's sarcoma
transmission: mother-to-child transmission during pregnancy and delivery
sharing contaminated needles, syringes and other injecting equipment
prevention: using a male or female condom during sex
being tested for HIV and other sexually transmitted infections
avoiding sharing contaminated needles, syringes and other injecting equipment
avoiding unsafe injections, blood transfusions, or tissue transplantation
risk_factors: having anal or vaginal sex without a condom
harmful use of alcohol or drugs in the context of sexual behaviour
sharing contaminated needles, syringes and other injecting equipment
receiving unsafe injections, blood transfusions, or tissue transplantation
complications: cancers such as lymphomas and Kaposi's sarcoma
key_facts: An estimated 44.1 million lives have been claimed by HIV to date
There were an estimated 40.8 million people living with HIV at the end of 2024
An estimated 630 000 people died from HIV-related causes in 2024
An estimated 1.3 million people acquired HIV in 2024
87% of people living with HIV knew their status in 2024
